target.title: fix(qa-lab): keep telegram QA progress detail truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QA Lab Telegram live progress output can contain malformed text when a detail message has emoji at the 240-character truncation boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bounded Telegram QA progress detail strings now use the existing UTF-16-safe truncation helper. The existing code-unit limit remains unchanged; this only backs a cut up to avoid splitting an emoji surrogate pair. No progress format, output prefix, or scenario behavior outside truncation changes.

## User Impact

Telegram QA progress details remain well-formed when scenario or canary diagnostics contain long emoji-containing values.

## Evidence

### Regression test crosses the actual cut
The test now uses a 236-code-unit ASCII prefix followed by emoji+after. With this input the emoji surrogate pair spans indices [236, 237] and current main raw `.slice(0, 237)` keeps only the high surrogate — the test **fails** on current main. The fixed path uses `truncateUtf16Safe(sanitized, 237)` which detects the split surrogate pair and backs up to index 236, producing 236 `a` chars + `...` (239 code units) with no lone surrogate.

### Terminal behavior proof (before vs. after)

**Before fix** (current main, raw `.slice(0, 237)`):
- Truncated: 236 `a` + lone high surrogate (U+D83D at index 236)
- Final output: 236 `a` + lone surrogate + `...` (240 code units)
- Lone surrogate detected: **yes** — emoji rendering breaks

**After fix** (`truncateUtf16Safe`):
- Truncated: 236 `a` (backed up to avoid splitting surrogate pair)
- Final output: 236 `a` + `...` (239 code units)
- Lone surrogate detected: **no** — emoji preserved cleanly

### Test suite
```
pnpm test extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/telegram/telegram-live.runtime.test.ts
✓ 45/45 passed
```

### Lint
```
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs
✓ clean
```

target.title: fix(gateway): classify chat error kind via canonical failover reasons
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The chat UI's `errorKind` badge was classified by `detectErrorKind` in `src/infra/errors.ts` — a naive substring detector (`message.includes("429")`, `"rate limit"`, `"timeout"`, `"too many tokens"`) that independently re-derived the provider-failure fact the canonical failover stack already owns as a closed `FailoverReason` union. The two classifiers disagree today:

- A Groq TPM 413 ("too many tokens per minute") badge showed **`context_length`**, while failover classification correctly says **`rate_limit`** (its TPM hint explicitly rejects context overflow). Same error, opposite user-facing kinds.
- "quota exceeded" / "resource_exhausted" / CJK rate-limit strings, "fetch failed" / "socket hang up", and 429s present only on a nested `response.status` all classified as unknown in chat while failover classifies them correctly.

This is seam 5 (error → user-facing failure classification) of #104219, slice 1: delete the driftiest duplicate and migrate its single consumer to the canonical owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ErrorKind` + `detectErrorKind` are deleted from `src/infra/errors.ts` (also removing provider-taxonomy leakage from `infra/`). The only prod consumer, `src/gateway/server-chat.ts`, now maps `resolveFailoverReasonFromError` into the protocol's chat kind set (`rate_limit|overloaded → rate_limit`, `context_overflow → context_length`), gates the `timeout` badge on the established `isTimeoutError` predicate (FailoverReason `timeout` is the retryable-transient bucket and deliberately swallows generic 5xx, so it cannot drive a user-facing timeout badge), and keeps refusal as a chat-local check — refusal is a model stop-reason fact, not a `FailoverReason`, so the failover union is not widened. The chat kind type is now derived from the gateway-protocol `ChatEvent` schema type instead of a re-declared union; the protocol schema itself is unchanged, and the gateway→agents import direction already exists (`openai-compat-errors.ts`, `server-methods/agent.ts`).

Named follow-up slices (out of scope here, tracked on #104219): fold the private 429-status-walk/conversation-state/internal-error detectors in `provider-request-error-classifier.ts` into the canonical module; unify the duplicated timeout-code sets; remove `agent-runner-execution.ts`'s raw-message re-checks.

## User Impact

Chat/web-UI error badges become consistent with failover classification: TPM rate limits show `rate_limit` instead of `context_length`; quota, overload, CJK rate-limit, and timeout-shaped failures show `rate_limit`/`timeout` instead of unknown, while generic HTTP 5xx stays unclassified rather than mislabeled. Conversely, bare "too many tokens"/"token limit" text without real overflow phrasing no longer over-matches to `context_length`. Diagnostics/UI only — no control-flow, retry, or delivery change. The ACP translator's `errorKind === "refusal"` → `stopReason` mapping is unaffected.

Shipped-API compatibility: `ErrorKind`/`detectErrorKind` are reachable from the latest stable package via the deprecated `openclaw/plugin-sdk/infra-runtime` subpath, so they are preserved there as `@deprecated` compat exports (old substring semantics, hosted in the barrel itself, zero core-runtime callers, removal planned with the next plugin-SDK major). Plugin-SDK surface pins are unchanged as a result.

## Evidence

- Drift sites: `src/infra/errors.ts:150-187` (deleted) vs canonical `src/agents/failover-error.ts` `resolveFailoverReasonFromError` + `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/failover-matches.ts` hint tables.
- Upstream trace: no prod producer sets lifecycle `data.errorKind` in the chat taxonomy today (`readChatErrorKind` remains a protocol-shaped validator), so the mapping is the sole classification path.
- Tests: table-driven mapping coverage in `src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts` (12 cases: the Groq TPM 413 drift regression, quota/resource_exhausted, http 429, fetch failed/socket hang up/etimedout, context overflow, refusal strings, plain error → omitted); `detectErrorKind` unit tests deleted with the function, equivalent cases migrated.
- `git diff --numstat`: net prod **−5 LOC** (`infra/errors.ts` −39, `server-chat.ts` +34).
- Local: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm check:import-cycles`, `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check`, focused vitest (282 tests), oxfmt — green.
- Remote (Blacksmith Testbox): `pnpm check:changed` exit 0. `pnpm test:changed` hit two known flaky groups under full shard load (`model-fallback.probe` async log-capture — same flake documented on #104319 — and `bash-tools.exec-runtime` suspension-timing tests, unrelated to this diff); all three suites pass isolated on the same lease (305/305).

### Real behavior proof (ephemeral gateway, real WS chat client)

Built worktree, ephemeral gateway (temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`), single provider `mockllm/mock-1` with no fallbacks so failures surface to chat, and a real gateway-protocol WS client (device-key `connect` + `chat.send`, capturing `event: "chat"` frames). Three scenarios, chat error events captured verbatim (redacted):

- HTTP 413 with Groq-style "too many tokens per minute" body -> chat error event `errorKind: "rate_limit"` (previously `context_length` via the deleted substring detector).
- HTTP 500 "Internal server error" -> chat error event with **no** `errorKind` (unknown badge; the review's regression case — not `timeout`).
- Timeout-shaped provider failure -> chat error event `errorKind: "timeout"`.

Classification path exercised end to end: `resolveChatErrorKindFromError` (`src/gateway/server-chat.ts`) on real gateway chat events, canonical reasons for rate-limit/overload/context, `isTimeoutError` gating the timeout badge (FailoverReason `timeout` is the retryable-transient bucket and deliberately swallows generic 5xx, so it cannot drive the badge).

Part of #104219 (seam 5: error classification, slice 1 of ~4).

target.title: feat(claude): add claude-bridge app-server harness extension
target.body:
## Summary

TL;DR:
Inspiration: https://openclaw.ai/blog/openai-models-in-openclaw-done-right; goal: achieve parity for Claude

New feature; issue https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/93793

OpenClaw currently has no first-class harness for Anthropic models. Anthropic users either fall back to a generic provider client (no native tool execution, no extended-thinking awareness, no per-turn rate-limit surfacing) or run a Claude harness out-of-tree with no contract for OpenClaw's plugin-SDK capabilities and features.

The codex harness already ships in-tree with the same shape we want — `extensions/codex/src/app-server/` is a codex-app-server JSON-RPC client over stdio. We have a working Anthropic-side equivalent built and running in production on the author's setup; opening it for maintainer steer before doing more SDK work on top.

Harness: this PR
JSON-RPC server: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge

**What is the intended outcome?**

- Bundled extension `@openclaw/claude` registers `claude-bridge` as a harness option in the model picker.
- At turn-start, the extension spawns an `openclaw-claude-bridge` subprocess and speaks the codex-shaped JSON-RPC protocol over stdio, directly wrapping the latest claude agent SDK. The server (currently published as `@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge`  https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge — fork-preview path; would migrate to `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` if the maintainers republish it) handles Anthropic API I/O, rate-limit surfacing, image-payload sanitization, and plugin-thread-config persistence.
- Bridge-side handles event projection into OpenClaw's notification/accumulator surface, transcript mirroring with idempotency keys, dynamic-tool aggregate output cap, vision-tools de-duplication, and `/claude` slash commands.
- See `extensions/claude/README.md` for the full feature map.

**What is intentionally out of scope?**

- Republishing the server under `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` — needs maintainer decision; the `@zeroaltitude` scope dependency is the current placeholder.
- Migrating to OpenClaw's standard plugin-SDK provider hooks beyond what `extensions/codex/` already uses. The bridge follows codex's pattern verbatim where applicable.
- Anything outside the harness bridge surface.

**What does success look like?** Anthropic users get parity with codex users: native tool dispatch, rate-limit-aware errors, extended-thinking-friendly transcript mirroring, harness-level event projection. No regressions to existing harnesses.

**What should reviewers focus on?**

1. **Scope concern — am I taking too much core?** The branch touches `src/plugins/command-registration.ts`, `src/plugins/current-plugin-metadata-snapshot.ts`, `src/plugins/agent-tool-result-middleware-types.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-native-slash-fast-path.ts`, `src/agents/model-runtime-aliases.ts`, and `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts`. Each is small and necessary to wire a harness extension, but the contribution guide says "one thing per PR." Happy to split into prep PRs first if maintainers prefer.
2. **External-plugin vs. bundled-extension** — Per CONTRIBUTING.md "most features should be third-party plugins." Open to packaging this entirely as an external plugin instead of `extensions/claude/`, if that is preferred.
3. **Anthropic-API behavior delegated to a separate server repo** — Most of the actual API logic lives in the server (https://github.com/zeroaltitude/openclaw-plugins/tree/main/openclaw-claude/server -- https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge). Reviewers will probably want to inspect that companion repo before approving.
4. **`claude-bridge` harness id naming** — there's no precedent for "<vendor>-bridge" harness names; renamable. (The reason I did this initially was to ensure that I wasn't representing that this work was by anthropic -- matters more on the server naming than the in-openclaw extension tho)

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Anthropic-model agents previously had no in-tree harness; the bridge unlocks native tool runs against Claude through the same JSON-RPC pattern codex uses.
- **Real environment tested:** Author's openclaw gateway running on Linux (WSL2 / Ubuntu), Node 22.x. Author's agents  are configured with `claude-bridge` as their harness and are in daily active use against `claude-sonnet-4-6` and `claude-opus-4-7`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `pnpm install && pnpm build`
  2. `openclaw gateway restart --deep`
  3. Send a Slack DM to one of the claude-bridge agents
  4. Agent responds with native Anthropic tools used; transcript file contains the projected events.
  5. `/claude status` in the same thread prints shared-client liveness.
- **Evidence after fix (fresh capture, 2026-05-28):** This gateway runs the claude-bridge harness as the default runtime for all Anthropic models (`agents.defaults.models.*.agentRuntime.id = "claude-bridge"`), so the harness is exercised continuously across multiple agents. Captured live:
  1. **Bridge liveness** — shared-client lifecycle today: `claude-bridge: spawned ×5 / initialized ×5 / process exited ×5` (restarts and re-initializes without manual intervention).
  2. **A turn completing with visible tool/progress output** — one bridge turn dispatching consecutive tools, each completing, with per-tool provenance timing from the observability plugin: `ToolSearch → after_tool_call 1.9ms`, `exec → 1.7ms`, `Write → 1.9ms`, `Agent → 1.9ms`.
  3. **Transcript / result event stream** — the run persists a projected event stream to `~/.openclaw/agents/<id>/sessions/<uuid>.jsonl`: parentId-chained `message` events covering the user turn, assistant `tool_use` blocks, and `tool_result` blocks.
  4. **`/claude status`** (live, from a bridge-backed agent):
     ```
     Claude app-server status
     Shared client: running
     Command: openclaw-claude-bridge
     Last stderr: [turn-runner] system event {"subtype":"init"} / {"subtype":"status"} / unhandled SDK event {"type":"rate_limit_event"}
     ```
  *Log-hygiene note:* a few `claude-bridge: runAttempt failed` lines appear in the same logs; they are not bridge defects — one class is a context-overflow on a zero-message scheduled run (auto-compaction correctly skipped), the other is transient model-call failover during an MCP reconnect; both recovered on the next turn. Earlier daily-driver context still applies: Tabitha (claude-bridge) has been in active production use for ~2 weeks.
- **Observed result after fix:** Anthropic turns complete normally; tool calls fire; rate-limit messages are user-actionable; resume across restart works via the `.claude-binding.json` sidecar.
- **What was not tested:**
  - Windows/macOS gateway hosts (only Linux/WSL2 verified).
  - Bun runtime (Node 22 only).
  - Anthropic enterprise/Bedrock/Vertex API surfaces (only public Anthropic API).
  - Concurrent multi-account scenarios beyond 3 agents.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** Author runs a single-host gateway. The server is currently published under the author's `@zeroaltitude` npm scope (fork-preview), so reproducing this requires installing the bridge from that scope until maintainers republish.
- **Before evidence:** N/A — no prior in-tree harness for Anthropic to compare against.

## Tests and validation

- Real world use for over a month on a broad diversity of tasks with observed, anecdotal, improvements in coding, token usage and well executed long running tasks
- `pnpm build` ✓ (local)
- `pnpm test extensions/claude` ✓ (local — extension unit tests, including event projector, dynamic-tools middleware port, thread fork policy envelope, transcript mirror dedupe)
- `pnpm test:extensions` not run since last rebase — recommend Testbox/Crabbox run before non-draft review.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` edit per contributor rule; maintainer to add on land.

## Risk checklist

- **Did user-visible behavior change?** Yes — new `claude-bridge` harness appears in model picker; new `/claude` slash command surface.
- **Did config, environment, or migration behavior change?** Yes — new plugin `configSchema` (see `extensions/claude/openclaw.plugin.json`). Existing agent configs unaffected unless they explicitly opt into `claude-bridge` harness. Doctor contract added (`extensions/claude/doctor-contract-api.ts`).
- **Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change?** Yes (intentional). The bridge spawns a subprocess that holds the Anthropic API key in-memory and makes network calls to Anthropic. Subprocess lifecycle is owned by the harness, not user shell. The plugin SDK enabler changes (e.g. `command-registration.ts`) are additive and follow existing codex-extension precedent.
- **Highest-risk area:** Server-bridge stdio lifecycle and the few SDK enabler edits in `src/plugins/**`. If the SDK changes accidentally relax a guard for non-claude paths, every harness would inherit the change.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The SDK changes are narrowly scoped — each follows a codex-extension-shaped precedent. Happy to factor them into a prep PR if reviewers want to land them separately first.

## Current review state

- **Next action:** Maintainer steer on scope: (a) accept as bundled extension as-is, (b) split SDK enablers into a prep PR first, or (c) request packaging as an external plugin.
- **Still waiting on:** Maintainer decision on the above. CI run on this push.
- **Bot/reviewer comments addressed:** None yet — opening draft.

---

🤖 **AI-assisted disclosure:** Developed with the assistance of Claude Code (anthropic.com/claude-code). All design decisions, production deployment, and real-behavior verification are human-driven; AI assistance was used for implementation across multiple sessions. Session transcripts available on request.

target.title: feat(android): add system share target
target.body:
Closes #104568

## What Problem This Solves

Android users cannot currently select OpenClaw from the system Sharesheet, so moving a link, text snippet, or photo into chat requires manual copy/paste or saving and reselecting the image. This leaves Android without the cross-app share entry point already available on iOS.

## Why This Change Was Made

This registers the existing MainActivity for text and image shares, normalizes ACTION_SEND and ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE payloads into a one-shot chat draft, and reuses the existing image compressor, composer, and durable outbox path. Shared content is never sent automatically: the user can review, edit, remove attachments, and explicitly tap Send. Warm shares prepend incoming text and append incoming images so existing unsent text and attachments remain intact. External image input is limited to eight provider-backed content URIs; file URIs are rejected to avoid a confused-deputy read of app-private files.

## User Impact

Android users can now share text, links, one image, or multiple images from browsers, photo apps, and other Android apps directly into the OpenClaw chat composer. Repeated shares reuse the foreground activity instead of stacking duplicate MainActivity instances, and a populated composer keeps its existing draft and attachments.

## Evidence

Validated on head bf2cfd45613f43585f1092f1df22a6b9eca15441:

- android-test-play passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29161496993/job/86567278430
- android-test-third-party passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29161496993/job/86567278420
- android-build-play passed, including both debug APK assemblies and Android lint: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29161496993/job/86567278449
- android-ktlint passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29161496993/job/86567278459
- native-i18n passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29161496993/job/86567278379
- Focused Robolectric coverage in apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/ShareLaunchTest.kt covers text composition, single and multiple images, ClipData fallback, URI bounds, and file URI rejection. apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/chat/ChatComposerDraftTest.kt covers preservation of populated and image-only composer drafts.
- cd apps/android && ./gradlew :app:ktlintFormat completed successfully.
- node --import tsx scripts/native-app-i18n.ts sync --write followed by check completed successfully.
- git diff --check is clean.
- Final .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output was clean with no accepted/actionable findings (Codex Sol/high, confidence 0.93).

Real-behavior evidence is still pending: no emulator or physical-device Sharesheet recording has been attached yet. The requested proof must show cold and warm text/image shares, URI-backed image import, preservation of a populated composer, and explicit user confirmation before send.

AI-assisted: yes. The implementation and tests were reviewed against the Android Sharesheet contract, review feedback, and the existing OpenClaw Android composer/outbox flow.

target.title: feat(fleet): multi-tenant hosting via openclaw fleet cell supervisor
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's trust model is one trusted operator domain per gateway: all agents, plugins, and Codex app-servers share one Node process, one OS user, and one shared-secret gateway credential. Operators who want to host agents for multiple users have no supported deployment shape, and in-process separation cannot become one — tenant plugins and Codex installs are arbitrary code running with the whole gateway's authority. Closes #104436.

## Why This Change Was Made

Treat the container boundary as the tenant boundary and keep every tenant a normal single-operator OpenClaw. This PR adds the v1 supervisor:

- `openclaw fleet create|list|status|start|stop|restart|upgrade|rm` — provisions one **cell** (a complete OpenClaw instance from the official `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw` image) per tenant, on Docker or Podman.
- Hardened container profile, asserted by tests both positively and negatively: `--cap-drop=ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, `--init`, PID/memory/CPU limits, `--restart unless-stopped`, per-cell bridge network, gateway port published on `127.0.0.1` only; never `docker.sock`, `--privileged`, host networking, or added capabilities.
- Cell state and auth-profile secrets mount at the paths the Docker install docs pin (`/home/node/.openclaw`, `/home/node/.config/openclaw`); user mapping handles rootful/rootless Docker and Podman `keep-id`, with SELinux `:Z` relabeling when active.
- The gateway token travels via a mode-0600 env-file (never argv), is redacted from error output, lives only in container env (not SQLite), and is carried over on `upgrade` from container inspection.
- Registry is a `fleet_cells` table in the shared state DB (Kysely; same zero-config-key pattern as managed worktrees). Per-tenant operation leases reuse the existing `state_leases` table so concurrent CLI mutations of one cell fail fast instead of corrupting container state; failed `create` rolls back only its own attempt-labeled artifacts, and failed `upgrade` restores the previous container.
- `rm --purge-data` requires `--force` and performs realpath containment checks (symlink-swap and sibling-cell escapes refused) before deleting anything.
- Docs: a new multi-tenant hosting concept page with an explicit trust statement (tenancy protects tenants from each other; the operator/host is trusted; host-compromise resistance is a non-goal), an isolation ladder (hardened container → gVisor/Kata/microVM → separate machines), and a `fleet` CLI reference. Shared channel ingress, slim per-tenant hosts, remote cells, and a tenant portal are explicitly deferred.

No gateway/runtime behavior changes, no new `openclaw.json` keys, no new dependencies; personal-mode deployments are untouched.

## User Impact

Operators get a supported, documented way to host multiple users on one Linux host with a real isolation story and lifecycle UX (`create` prints the cell URL and one-time gateway token). Existing single-operator deployments see no behavior change.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: 120 passed (7 files) on Blacksmith Testbox at the final head, Actions run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29157009109 (earlier heads: 115/118 passed, runs 29156227026 and 29156762499)
- Changed-lanes gate (`pnpm check:changed`) on Blacksmith Testbox: all lanes green except "test temp creation report", which crashes on the delegated sync checkout with `fatal: origin/main...HEAD: no merge base` — an infrastructure issue unrelated to this diff (the same report over this diff locally returns zero findings in both branch and staged mode); harness fix tracked separately.
- Full `pnpm build` clean, no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` findings.
- Docs checks: `docs:map` regenerated; docs link check passed (5,849 links, 0 broken) in the Codex build pass.
- Structured autoreview (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, xhigh) per commit: the test and docs commits reviewed clean apart from accepted findings that are fixed in the follow-up commit; the feat commit surfaced two real P2s — upgrades could commit an immediately-crashing replacement without triggering restore, and a name collision with an unlabeled foreign container/network stranded the tenant reservation unrecoverably. Both fixed (replacement now verified by attempt-label + running-state inspection before the registry update; unlabeled resources treated as provably foreign: left untouched, reservation released) plus five new regression tests; the docs finding (`unknown` state also signals ownership mismatch) is documented. A second review round hardened the upgrade gate further: commit now waits for the replacement to answer `/healthz` (the compose health contract) with fast-fail on exit/restart-loop and a bounded ~60s deadline before restore, so a start-then-crash image cannot displace a healthy cell. Final fix commit reviewed clean ("no accepted/actionable findings", confidence 0.94).
- Design provenance: adversarially reviewed architecture discussion (cells over in-process RBAC), see #104436 for the threat-model rationale.

target.title: feat(onboarding): add provider sign-in
target.body:
Closes #104424

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw onboarding could detect local AI tools and accept API keys, but the macOS flow could not guide users through provider-managed sign-in. Provider failures were also difficult to inspect or copy, the setup dialog underused its available space, and the Claude Code/Codex presentation implied a preference when both were usable.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one generic, manifest-driven provider-auth wizard shared by CLI and macOS onboarding. It supports OpenAI ChatGPT OAuth and device code, OpenRouter OAuth, GitHub Copilot, Google Gemini CLI, xAI, MiniMax global/CN, and Chutes while keeping provider-specific auth in each provider plugin. Credentials are staged, live-probed, and persisted only after success; cancellation, reconnect, terminal-error, rollback, and late-response races are handled at the wizard boundary.

Provider sign-in URLs are now structured wizard data instead of text inferred from prompts. The macOS client validates those URLs, opens each one at most once, and keeps an explicit link visible for retry or manual use.

The macOS page now uses the available dialog space, exposes friendly errors with expandable copyable details, omits the AI-powered Crestodian when no inference is configured, uses bundled vector artwork for Claude Code and Codex, and makes an unbiased randomized choice when both local CLIs work.

## User Impact

Users can sign in to supported providers without manually finding and pasting an API key, while retaining key-based setup where providers support it. Setup errors remain visible and copyable, provider sign-in can be safely cancelled or retried, and the macOS onboarding page presents local CLI choices without favoring Claude Code or Codex.

target.body:
Closes #104543

AI-assisted

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users viewing a long Control UI chat transcript would only see the first `chat.history` page (limit 100) and could expand only within that already-loaded window. Scrolling to the top never requested older transcript pages, so prior messages on the server looked missing even though `chat.history` already supports `offset` / `nextOffset` / `hasMore` / `totalMessages`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI now requests the first history page with `offset: 0` so pagination metadata is returned, keeps the cursor on chat state, and fetches the next older page when the user scrolls to the top after the local render window is exhausted. Older messages are prepended with scroll-anchor preservation, and the hidden-history notice distinguishes locally unrendered loaded messages from older server pages that have not been fetched yet.

## User Impact

On long sessions, scrolling near the top of the transcript loads older messages from the gateway instead of stopping at the first 100. The history notice makes it clear when more messages still exist on the server.

target.title: fix(tlon): clear SSE connect timeout after failed openStream
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Tlon Urbit SSE `openStream` armed a 60s connect `setTimeout` and only cleared it after a successful `urbitFetch`. When the connect fetch rejected (DNS/SSRF/network), the timer stayed armed until it fired, and reconnect storms could stack dangling timers in the Gateway process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrap the connect fetch in `try/finally` and always `clearTimeout`, matching the zalouser probe timeout cleanup pattern, so failed connects release the timer immediately without changing the connect deadline or stream lifecycle.

## User Impact

Flaky Urbit hosts no longer leave dangling connect timers in long-running Tlon monitors during reconnect failures.

## Evidence

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/sse-client.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Failed SSE connect attempts no longer leave uncleared 60s AbortController timers.
- **Canonical reachability path:** Tlon monitor reconnect → `UrbitSSEClient.openStream` → `urbitFetch` reject/non-OK → `finally { clearTimeout(timeoutId) }`.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; fake timers + mocked `urbitFetch` exercise the production `openStream` caller.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): keep telegram QA progress detail truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QA Lab Telegram live progress output can contain malformed text when a detail message has emoji at the 240-character truncation boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bounded Telegram QA progress detail strings now use the existing UTF-16-safe truncation helper. The existing code-unit limit remains unchanged; this only backs a cut up to avoid splitting an emoji surrogate pair. No progress format, output prefix, or scenario behavior outside truncation changes.

## User Impact

Telegram QA progress details remain well-formed when scenario or canary diagnostics contain long emoji-containing values.

## Evidence

### Regression test crosses the actual cut
The test now uses a 236-code-unit ASCII prefix followed by emoji+after. With this input the emoji surrogate pair spans indices [236, 237] and current main raw `.slice(0, 237)` keeps only the high surrogate — the test **fails** on current main. The fixed path uses `truncateUtf16Safe(sanitized, 237)` which detects the split surrogate pair and backs up to index 236, producing 236 `a` chars + `...` (239 code units) with no lone surrogate.

### Terminal behavior proof (before vs. after)

**Before fix** (current main, raw `.slice(0, 237)`):
- Truncated: 236 `a` + lone high surrogate (U+D83D at index 236)
- Final output: 236 `a` + lone surrogate + `...` (240 code units)
- Lone surrogate detected: **yes** — emoji rendering breaks

**After fix** (`truncateUtf16Safe`):
- Truncated: 236 `a` (backed up to avoid splitting surrogate pair)
- Final output: 236 `a` + `...` (239 code units)
- Lone surrogate detected: **no** — emoji preserved cleanly

### Test suite
```
pnpm test extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/telegram/telegram-live.runtime.test.ts
✓ 45/45 passed
```

### Lint
```
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs
✓ clean
```

target.title: fix(browser): reject loose click coordinate numbers when normalizing actions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Browser action requests could accept loose coordinate numbers for `clickCoords`, such as hexadecimal or exponent-form strings, when users or tools submit direct coordinate clicks through the browser `/act` workflow.

## Why This Change Was Made

`clickCoords` now uses one browser-owned decimal-only finite coordinate parser from both the CLI and the `/act` route before dispatch, matching the Browser CLI contract that allows fractional CSS-pixel coordinates while rejecting non-decimal numeric syntax. This is an owner-local browser route/CLI normalization fix only; it does not add config, compatibility aliases, or provider behavior.

## User Impact

Browser action callers get consistent validation for coordinate clicks: decimal and fractional coordinates continue to work, while hexadecimal and exponent-form strings are rejected before malformed coordinate clicks are dispatched.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: Browser `/act` route normalization and the Browser CLI now share one decimal-only `clickCoords` parser, preserve decimal/fractional coordinates, reject loose numeric strings, and avoid dispatching malformed coordinate clicks.
- Current PR head: `6de51742e99864f83357adbc7f738b1158fe09de`; matching proof tree: `2a9fe51c86ff23a89a47addba253a4a6928d53d2`.
- Conflict/parser repair: merged current `main` into the PR branch, resolved the Browser route overlap, and moved the decimal coordinate grammar into `extensions/browser/src/browser/click-coordinate.ts` so `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.normalize.ts` and `extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/register.element.ts` share the same parser.
- Current-head checks:
  - GitHub `Real behavior proof` passed on the current head: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29161445172/job/86567099365.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.normalize.test.ts extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/register.element.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server.agent-contract-core.test.ts --testNamePattern "clickCoords|coordinate|click-coords|numeric fields"` passed with 11 tests passing and 37 skipped.
  - `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
  - `python .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Earlier real Browser `/act` setup proof for this behavior path: a temporary no-repo-change proof script launched a fresh headless Chrome profile with remote debugging, started the product Browser control routes through `registerBrowserRoutes` and `createBrowserRouteContext`, opened a local HTML page, and posted directly to the real `/act` HTTP route. The successful fractional request went through Playwright and incremented the page's click counter; the rejected hexadecimal and exponent requests returned before dispatch, leaving the counter unchanged.

```text
Browser /act real setup proof (head 31a4da266410c811419e3d2d2089f5da1c25d28c; behavior preserved by the current-head shared-parser repair above)
Chrome CDP: http://127.0.0.1:65204 (temporary headless Chrome profile)
Browser control: http://127.0.0.1:65206
Test page: http://127.0.0.1:65205/proof
Opened targetId: 31A5A133CA7CFBCE07B9F4B47893361B
fractional clickCoords status/body: 200 {"ok":true,"targetId":"31A5A133CA7CFBCE07B9F4B47893361B","url":"http://127.0.0.1:65205/proof"}
click state after fractional: 200 {"ok":true,"targetId":"31A5A133CA7CFBCE07B9F4B47893361B","url":"http://127.0.0.1:65205/proof","result":{"clicks":1,"last":{"x":42,"y":44,"target":"target"}}}
hex clickCoords status/body: 400 {"error":"clickCoords requires non-negative x and y","code":"ACT_INVALID_REQUEST"}
exponent clickCoords status/body: 400 {"error":"clickCoords requires non-negative x and y","code":"ACT_INVALID_REQUEST"}
click state after rejected inputs: 200 {"ok":true,"targetId":"31A5A133CA7CFBCE07B9F4B47893361B","url":"http://127.0.0.1:65205/proof","result":{"clicks":1}}
```

- Observed result: normalization accepts decimal fractional strings such as `x: "10.5", y: ".25"`; the CLI rejects non-decimal coordinate arguments before sending `/act`; and `/act` returns `ACT_INVALID_REQUEST` with `clickCoords requires non-negative x and y` for negative, hexadecimal, and exponent-form coordinate inputs before malformed clicks are dispatched.

target.title: fix(admin-http-rpc): time out incomplete request bodies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where authenticated Admin HTTP RPC callers could leave an incomplete request body open and keep `POST /api/v1/admin/rpc` waiting before the request is rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admin HTTP RPC now uses a response-safe bounded JSON body reader at the route boundary: timeout and size failures stop body consumption, flush the JSON HTTP error response, and then close the request connection. This preserves the existing 1 MiB size limit and invalid-JSON messages, stays within the admin-http-rpc plugin route, and does not change the method allowlist, auth model, config, or dispatch behavior.

## User Impact

Trusted host automation receives a delivered HTTP 408 JSON response for incomplete request bodies instead of leaving the Admin HTTP RPC request pending indefinitely or losing the timeout response when the socket closes.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: incomplete Admin HTTP RPC request bodies time out before gateway dispatch, and a real partial-body HTTP client receives the JSON 408 before the connection closes.
- Current-head proof at `6ef40b353c04c9413b545021a5dca22f9ded2ab7`:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/admin-http-rpc/src/handler.test.ts` passed with 13 tests passing, including the raw-socket partial-body regression.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/http-body.test.ts` passed with 13 tests passing.
  - Real HTTP socket proof against `handleAdminHttpRpcRequest` produced:

```text
status=HTTP/1.1 408 Request Timeout
connection: close
body={"ok":false,"error":{"type":"invalid_request","message":"Request body timeout"}}
```

- Committed diff hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode commit --commit HEAD --model gpt-5.6-terra` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result: the focused regression returns HTTP 408 with `Request body timeout`, the real socket receives that JSON response before close, and `dispatchGatewayMethod` is not called for the incomplete body.

commands.author: yetval

target.title: fix(agents): protect provider auth exchange output by sensitivity, not input marker
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`protectPreparedProviderRuntimeAuth` (`src/agents/provider-secret-egress.ts`) is the guard that
re-sentinels credentials returned by a provider auth exchange so real tokens are never stored or
logged in the clear. It decided *whether* to protect from the shape of the INPUT `sourceApiKey`: if
that input was not already a sentinel and not registered for redaction, it returned the exchange
OUTPUT completely untouched. That assumes output sensitivity mirrors input sensitivity, which is
false for any provider that turns a non-secret marker into a real credential.

The bundled `amazon-bedrock-mantle` plugin is a live instance:

- Its stored config `apiKey` is the marker `__amazon_bedrock_mantle_iam__`
  (`extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.ts`), which the plugin manifest does NOT declare in
  `nonSecretAuthMarkers`, so `resolveUsableCustomProviderApiKey` returns it raw as the source key.
- At request time `prepareRuntimeAuth` -> `resolveMantleRuntimeBearerToken` mints a real IAM-derived
  Bedrock bearer token (`bedrock-api-key-...`).
- That real token passed through the guard unprotected because the source marker is neither a
  sentinel nor registered.

In any environment using implicit mantle auth (no explicit `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, ambient AWS
credentials present) the generated bearer token flowed through auth storage and request headers
unencrypted and unregistered for redaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fix the guard at its own ownership boundary: protect based on OUTPUT sensitivity, which is the
function's documented job ("Re-sentinels credentials returned by a provider auth exchange").

Before:

```ts
if (
  !looksLikeSecretSentinel(params.sourceApiKey) &&
  !isSecretValueRegisteredForRedaction(params.sourceApiKey)
) {
  return preparedAuth;
}
const protect = (value, label) => protectRuntimeAuthValue({ value, provider: params.provider, label });
```

After:

```ts
const protect = (value: string, label: string): string =>
  !value || isNonSecretApiKeyMarker(value)
    ? value
    : protectRuntimeAuthValue({ value, provider: params.provider, label });
```

The input-based short-circuit and the now-dead `sourceApiKey` parameter are removed. Protection is
gated per output value: skip empty values and non-secret markers, protect everything else.
`protectRuntimeAuthValue` already skips values that are already sentinels.

The alternative of declaring `__amazon_bedrock_mantle_iam__` in the plugin's `nonSecretAuthMarkers`
was rejected: tracing `resolveUsableCustomProviderApiKey` shows that path would make it return
`null` for mantle (marker recognized -> skip raw-return -> not an env marker -> remote baseUrl fails
the local-provider branch -> `null`), breaking mantle auth; and even if it resolved, a non-secret
marker source would still fail the old guard, so the token would remain unprotected. Keying off
output sensitivity is the only fix that stops the leak and prevents recurrence for the next plugin.

Sibling providers are unaffected: lmstudio/ollama/codex/anthropic-vertex `prepareRuntimeAuth` echo
their own markers (`lmstudio-local`, `ollama-local`, `codex-app-server`, `gcp-vertex-credentials`),
all of which `isNonSecretApiKeyMarker` returns true for and are skipped. Only outputs that are real
credentials from a non-registered source (mantle) newly get protected. The apiKey-minting plus
egress-unwrap round-trip is already exercised today by the sentinel-source path, so no new unhandled
egress path is introduced.

`resolveUsableCustomProviderApiKey` returning inline `models.json` literal keys raw is a separate
classification quirk and is out of scope here; for mantle it is harmless (the marker is not itself a
secret; the real token is minted downstream and is what this PR protects).

## User Impact

Operators running implicit amazon-bedrock-mantle auth no longer have their IAM-derived Bedrock
bearer token stored or logged in plaintext; it is sentinel-wrapped in auth storage and headers and
registered for exact-value log redaction, matching every other provider whose auth exchange yields a
real credential. No config or plugin-author action required. No behavior change for providers that
return non-secret markers.

## Evidence

Verification (scoped, from a deps-enabled worktree at the same base):

- `run-vitest.mjs src/agents/provider-secret-egress.test.ts` -> 6 passed. The new regression
  assertion fails on pristine `main` (guard returns the raw token) and passes with the patch.
- `oxfmt --check` on the 7 changed files -> clean.
- `oxlint` on the 7 changed files -> clean.
- `run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` -> clean.

Novelty: #102009 (merged) introduced the process-local sentinel egress system and #102420 (merged)
added capture/retention hardening plus tests, but neither touches this input-vs-output guard, the
`model-auth-markers` path, or the mantle marker. #93952 (open) edits `auth-controller.ts` near this
call but changes the `RuntimeAuthState.sourceApiKey` field, not the `protectPreparedProviderRuntimeAuth`
call; a trivial rebase may be needed if it lands first.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: with implicit amazon-bedrock-mantle auth, the IAM-derived Bedrock bearer token minted by the plugin flows through protectPreparedProviderRuntimeAuth unprotected (not sentinel-wrapped, not registered for redaction).
Real environment tested: drove the real amazon-bedrock-mantle resolveMantleRuntimeBearerToken and the real protectPreparedProviderRuntimeAuth guard on pristine main 4b33199a and on the patched tree with identical inputs. Real: the mantle resolver, the MANTLE_IAM_TOKEN_MARKER constant, region resolution, sentinel minting, and the secret-redaction registry. The only external seam was the injected AWS token provider factory, standing in for the @aws/bedrock-token-generator IAM network call.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: called resolveMantleRuntimeBearerToken({ apiKey: MANTLE_IAM_TOKEN_MARKER, env: { AWS_REGION: "us-east-1" }, tokenProviderFactory: () => async () => "bedrock-api-key-PROOFTOKEN" }) to mint the real token, then passed the result through protectPreparedProviderRuntimeAuth for provider amazon-bedrock-mantle, and printed the guard output apiKey, whether it is a sentinel placeholder, and whether the raw token is registered for redaction.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 4b33199a)
mantle resolver minted apiKey: bedrock-api-key-PROOFTOKEN
guard output apiKey: bedrock-api-key-PROOFTOKEN
guard output apiKey is a sentinel placeholder: false
real token registered for redaction: false
# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
mantle resolver minted apiKey: bedrock-api-key-PROOFTOKEN
guard output apiKey: oc-sent-v2.ncxUhekdrlTvEHc6l2OuRuoqm_hglZgliAdD2QBRh9_tH_t7K2xVTks-K4DZNNcW7X9gYgncqgYEavBAJws.end
guard output apiKey is a sentinel placeholder: true
real token registered for redaction: true
```
Observed result after fix: the same real Bedrock bearer token that leaked in the clear before is now replaced by a sentinel placeholder in the guard output and registered for exact-value redaction, while the mantle resolver output feeding the guard is byte-identical across both runs.
What was not tested: no live AWS IAM call (the token provider factory was injected in place of the network round-trip); the full build was not run.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(msteams): add timeouts to SharePoint file send requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes MS Teams group/channel file sends that could hang indefinitely when SharePoint upload, sharing-link creation, chat-member lookup, or drive-item metadata requests stalled before headers or while reading response bodies.

## Why This Change Was Made

The affected SharePoint/Graph calls now use an aborting timeout around the full fetch lifecycle, including response body reads. The timeout helper lives in `extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts`, the existing MS Teams timeout owner.

The SharePoint content PUT now has a transfer-specific 5 minute deadline. Short Graph control-plane requests keep the existing 30 second MS Teams request timeout so stalled metadata/link/member calls still fail quickly without breaking slow but valid file uploads.

## User Impact

MS Teams group/channel file sends no longer remain pending forever when Microsoft Graph or SharePoint stops responding. Slow valid uploads get a transfer-sized deadline instead of being cut off at 30 seconds.

## Evidence

Exact head: `f1f83bfee4e451fe92226d76dc96082aff18707c`.

Implementation updates after ClawSweeper/CI review:

- Fixed CI lint failure `typescript(prefer-promise-reject-errors)` in `extensions/msteams/src/graph-upload.test.ts`.
- Moved the aborting timeout wrapper into `extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts`.

target.title: fix(agents): reject invalid goal token budgets
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where agents using `create_goal` with malformed `token_budget` values such as `"42.9"` or `"1abc"` could create a goal with a truncated numeric budget instead of getting an invalid-input error.

## Why This Change Was Made

`create_goal` now advertises `token_budget` as an integer with a minimum of 1 and uses the shared strict positive-integer reader at the model-facing tool boundary. Invalid present values are rejected before any session goal is created, while valid positive integer budgets keep the existing goal creation path.

## User Impact

Goal token budgets now match the documented positive-budget contract, so agents cannot silently create goals with a different budget than the value they supplied.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: malformed and non-positive `create_goal.token_budget` values are rejected by the real model-facing tool invocation, `get_goal` reads back no goal after those invalid calls, and a valid positive integer budget still creates an active goal.
- Current-head real behavior proof at `01d0a7d9c957675317d6a44d6a31e118e50e2786`: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -` imported `createCreateGoalTool`, `createGetGoalTool`, `upsertSessionEntry`, and `resolveStorePath`, seeded an isolated temp session row, then invoked the real `create_goal` and `get_goal` tool executors.

```json
{
  "head": "01d0a7d9c957675317d6a44d6a31e118e50e2786",
  "proofPath": [
    "upsertSessionEntry",
    "createCreateGoalTool",
    "create_goal.execute",
    "createGetGoalTool",
    "get_goal.execute"
  ],
  "invalidResults": [
    {
      "tokenBudget": "42.9",
      "rejected": true,
      "message": "token_budget must be a positive integer"
    },
    {
      "tokenBudget": "1abc",
      "rejected": true,
      "message": "token_budget must be a positive integer"
    },
    {
      "tokenBudget": 0,
      "rejected": true,
      "message": "token_budget must be a positive integer"
    }
  ],
  "afterInvalid": {
    "hasGoal": false,
    "status": "missing"
  },
  "validCreate": {
    "status": "created",
    "tokenBudget": 42
  },
  "afterValid": {
    "hasGoal": true,
    "objective": "prove valid budget still works",
    "tokenBudget": 42,
    "status": "active"
  },
  "assertions": {
    "invalidRejected": true,
    "invalidMessages": true,
    "noGoalAfterInvalid": true,
    "validBudgetStillCreatesGoal": true
  }
}
```

- Focused regression proof at `01d0a7d9c957675317d6a44d6a31e118e50e2786`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/goal-tools.test.ts` passed with 1 test file and 6 tests.
- Committed diff hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode commit --commit HEAD` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: fix(agents): distinguish z.ai code 1305 content rejection from generic overload
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: z.ai Coding Plan endpoint returns HTTP 429 with code 1305 deterministically when the system prompt contains "You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw". The current error classifier treats all 1305 responses as generic overload, showing "The AI service is temporarily overloaded" to users — which is misleading for the content-rejection case.

**Solution**: Add a `ZAI_CODE_1305_RE` pattern to detect `{"code":1305,...}` or `{"code":"1305",...}` (quoted or unquoted) in the raw error message and surface a more specific diagnostic before falling back to the generic overload message. The `classifyFailoverReason` hook in the z.ai plugin ensures code 1305 is classified as "overloaded" (provider-scoped), preventing misclassification by the generic rate-limit pattern.

**What changed**: 
- `sanitize-user-facing-text.ts`: Updated `ZAI_CODE_1305_RE` regex constant to match both `"code":1305` (unquoted number) and `"code":"1305"` (quoted string) JSON values; new check in `formatRateLimitOrOverloadedErrorCopy` that runs before `isOverloadedErrorMessage` and returns a neutral diagnostic for z.ai 1305 errors: "transient overload or a provider-side content restriction — try again later or with a different model."
- `extensions/zai/index.ts`: Added `classifyFailoverReason` hook that explicitly classifies z.ai code 1305 as "overloaded" (provider-scoped, prevents generic rate-limit classification from bypassing the diagnostic check)
- `failover-matches.test.ts`, `formatassistanterrortext.test.ts`: Updated tests to expect the new diagnostic message

**What did NOT change**:
- The `rate_limit` failover classification is preserved — backoff and fallback continue working
- Non-1305 overload errors return the original "overloaded" message unchanged
- Zhipu GLM `[1305]` format is not affected (doesn't match the JSON key pattern)

**Fixes**: #103529

## What Problem This Solves

Users onboarding a valid z.ai Coding Plan key successfully, but every chat turn fails with a misleading "overloaded" error. The real cause — the system prompt signature line triggering a provider-side content filter — is invisible. Users waste time checking quota, retrying, or switching API keys when the issue is the system prompt content.

## Root Cause

z.ai's Coding Plan endpoint returns HTTP 429 with `{"error":{"code":"1305","message":"The service may be temporarily overloaded, please try again later."}}` when the system message contains "You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw". This behavior is a **deterministic function of the system prompt content**, not a transient overload. Removing or altering that one line produces a 200 response.

The error classifier in `sanitize-user-facing-text.ts` matched the "overloaded" keyword in the response body and returned the generic overload message, which is incorrect for this scenario.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Error message for z.ai code 1305 now mentions possible content restriction instead of generic overload

**Real environment tested**: Node 24, macOS, tsx 4.19, vitest 4.1.9

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Direct call to `formatRateLimitOrOverloadedErrorCopy` (production function) via tsx — covering canonical payload, backward-compatible format, and non-1305 fallthrough.

**After-fix evidence**:
```terminal
$ node --import tsx zai-1305-evidence.ts
=== Part 1: Canonical payload ===
Input: {"error":{"code":"1305","message":"The service may be temporarily..."}}
Output: ⚠️ Provider returned code 1305. This can be a transient overload
or a provider-side content restriction — try again later or with a
different model.

=== Part 2: Backward compatible ===
Input: {"code":1305,"message":"..."}
Output: ⚠️ Provider returned code 1305. [same diagnostic]

=== Part 3: Non-1305 fallthrough ===
Generic overload: "The AI service is temporarily overloaded." ← unchanged
Rate limit with retry: "⚠️ rate limit: service overloaded..." ← preserved
Zhipu GLM [1305]: undefined ← not affected
Non-z.ai 429: "⚠️ API rate limit reached." ← passes through
```

**Observed result after the fix**: The diagnostic is more neutral — it covers both overload and content-rejection scenarios without misleading users toward "system prompt" guidance they cannot act on. Provider-scoping through the z.ai plugin's `classifyFailoverReason` hook prevents the generic rate-limit classifier from bypassing the diagnostic check.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end with a real z.ai API key (L3 full gateway run). The original issue (#103529) provides curl-level reproduction. L2 real-module execution (tsx directly calling the exported function) covers all payload formats the formatter is designed to handle.

## Tests and validation

**Exact steps or command run**: vitest run (32 + 90 + 15 tests)

**Test output**:
```terminal
✓ failover-matches.test.ts: 32 passed
✓ formatassistanterrortext.test.ts: 90 passed
✓ extensions/zai/index.test.ts: 15 passed
Total: 137 passed
```

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] Provider-scoped: z.ai plugin's classifyFailoverReason hook ensures code 1305 is only handled within z.ai provider context
- [x] Neutral diagnostic: "transient overload or content restriction" handles both scenarios without speculation
- [x] No change to failover/fallback behavior (rate_limit/overloaded classification preserved)
- [x] All 137 unit tests pass
- [x] 26 insertions, 8 deletions — within the Diamond Lobster 100-line limit

target.title: fix(google): stream Gemini batch JSONL output instead of res.text()
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a memory spike in the Gemini embedding batch download step where large batch output files are fully buffered in memory before any embedding is written to the result map.

`fetchGeminiFileContent` called `res.text()` to download the JSONL output file as a single string, then `parseGeminiBatchOutput` called `text.split("\n")` to produce a full `GeminiBatchOutputLine[]` array. Both the raw text buffer and the parsed object array exist simultaneously at peak — for a large embedding batch this roughly doubles peak heap on top of the result map.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the two-step buffer-then-parse approach with a streaming readline reader that consumes one JSONL line at a time and writes each embedding directly into `byCustomId`, matching the pattern already established in `extensions/voyage/embedding-batch.ts`.

Structural changes:

- **Deleted** `fetchGeminiFileContent` — returned the full JSONL body as a `string`.
- **Deleted** `parseGeminiBatchOutput` — split the string and mapped it to `GeminiBatchOutputLine[]`.
- **Added** `readGeminiBatchOutputContent` — wraps `Response.body` with `Readable.fromWeb` + `readline.Interface`, applies each line inline, and always closes/destroys reader resources in `finally`.
- **Added** `fetchGeminiBatchOutput` — thin wrapper that builds the `:download` URL and delegates body reading to the streamed reader.

Identifier precedence (`key` / `custom_id` / `request_id`) and both error paths are preserved.

## User Impact

Peak memory for large Gemini embedding batch jobs drops from roughly `2× output file size` (raw text + parsed lines + result map) toward approximately the embedding result map size. Successful batches, partial-error batches, and empty-output error paths keep the same user-visible behavior.

## Evidence

- Pattern parity with `extensions/voyage/embedding-batch.ts` streamed JSONL reader
- Focused regression: delayed mid-line chunked `ReadableStream` body through production `runGeminiEmbeddingBatches`
- Real `node:http` Transfer-Encoding chunked download against production caller with peak-heap before/after

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Gemini embedding batch download no longer holds the full JSONL text and a full parsed-line array in memory at the same time while populating `byCustomId`.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `runGeminiEmbeddingBatches` → `fetchGeminiBatchOutput` → `withRemoteHttpResponse` → `readGeminiBatchOutputContent` (`Readable.fromWeb` + `readline`) → per-line `byCustomId.set`.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; real Node `http.createServer` on `127.0.0.1` serving a ~22 MiB JSONL body with 22,823 on-wire chunks (no `Content-Length`), fetched through production SSRF-guarded `withRemoteHttpResponse` with `allowPrivateNetwork`.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Mirrors Voyage's provider-local streamed JSONL reader; no new config/env. Google Batch API output remains JSONL with per-line `key`/`response`/`error`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (darwin 24.3.0), Node 22 (`--expose-gc --import tsx`), branch `fix/gemini-batch-streaming-jsonl-reader`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ node --expose-gc --import tsx /tmp/gemini-batch-stream-proof.mjs
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google/embedding-batch.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
payload_lines= 12000
payload_bytes= 23370184
payload_mib= 22.29 MiB
chunk_bytes= 1024
gc_available= true
BEFORE_mode=res.text()+split+parse_all
BEFORE_buffered_count= 12000
BEFORE_buffered_text_bytes= 23370184
BEFORE_buffered_parsed_lines= 12000
BEFORE_peak_heap_delta= 61.84 MiB
BEFORE_peak_heap= 166.04 MiB
BEFORE_download_chunks= 22823
AFTER_mode=production_runGeminiEmbeddingBatches_readline_stream
AFTER_streamed_count= 12000
AFTER_streamed_sample_dims= 96
AFTER_peak_heap_delta= 24.32 MiB
AFTER_peak_heap= 132.46 MiB
AFTER_download_chunks= 22823
AFTER_download_bytes= 23370184
peak_delta_ratio_streamed_over_buffered= 0.393
peak_delta_saved= 37.52 MiB
proof_ok= true

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google/embedding-batch.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 ✓ bounds oversized file-upload JSON response and cancels the stream
 ✓ bounds oversized batch-create JSON response and cancels the stream
 ✓ bounds oversized batch-status poll JSON response and cancels the stream
 ✓ parses small responses on all three JSON paths correctly
 ✓ streams multi-line JSONL batch output across delayed chunks

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Same ~22.29 MiB JSONL payload was served in 22,823 delayed HTTP chunks. The old `res.text()` + split + parse-all path peaked at +61.84 MiB heap delta while retaining text + parsed lines + result map. Production `runGeminiEmbeddingBatches` on this branch resolved all 12,000 embeddings with +24.32 MiB peak delta (~39% of the buffered delta; ~37.5 MiB saved on this workload). Supplemental Vitest proves mid-line chunk boundaries across an async `ReadableStream`.
- **What was not tested:** Live Google Gemini Batch API credentials / real Files API download against Google infrastructure; process RSS via `/usr/bin/time` outside V8 heapUsed sampling.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

- Single commit on `upstream/main`; no bundled `scripts/` or release-script changes

target.title: Fix/OpenAI device code request timeout
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running OpenAI Codex device-code login (`openclaw models auth login --provider openai --device-code`, or the equivalent configure/wizard auth choice) could hang forever when a single `auth.openai.com` HTTP request stopped responding.

Before this patch, the flow only enforced a 15-minute poll-loop deadline around authorization waiting. The three `fetch` calls for user-code request, authorization poll, and token exchange had no per-request `AbortSignal` timeout, so a stalled TCP/proxy/blackhole response could bypass that deadline and leave the CLI spinner stuck. A server that returned headers and then stalled the body could also escape an incomplete timeout catch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Treat each device-code HTTP call as one timed operation: headers fetch plus bounded body read under the same `AbortSignal.timeout` (30s, aligned with the sibling ChatGPT browser OAuth token request timeout). Poll requests clamp that timeout to the remaining 15-minute authorization deadline and retry on per-operation timeout (including post-header body stalls) until the overall deadline expires. User-code and token-exchange timeouts fail fast with a clear error.

Scope stays OpenAI Codex device-code login HTTP only; browser OAuth and other providers are unchanged.

## User Impact

**Before:** A hung device-code HTTP request (or a post-header body stall) could block `models auth login --device-code` indefinitely, even past the advertised 15-minute authorization window.

**After:** Each device-code request+body read aborts after 30 seconds (or sooner near the overall deadline). Poll timeouts retry within the 15-minute window; user-code and token-exchange stalls surface an explicit timeout error instead of hanging forever.

## Evidence

- `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.ts` — one operation deadline for fetch + body read on user-code, poll, and token-exchange; poll retries on timeout within the 15-minute deadline
- Regression: `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.test.ts`
  - hung user-code aborts with timeout error
  - poll retries after `TimeoutError` and completes
  - hung token exchange aborts with timeout error
  - success path asserts all three fetches carry an `AbortSignal`
  - real `node:http` partial-body stall: user-code / token-exchange abort with formatted timeout; poll retries and succeeds

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** OpenAI Codex device-code login no longer leaves individual HTTP operations unbounded when the remote endpoint stops responding before headers return, or returns headers and then stalls the body.
- **Canonical reachability path:** Operator runs device-code auth → `loginOpenAICodexDeviceCode` → `requestOpenAICodexDeviceCode` / `pollOpenAICodexDeviceCode` / `exchangeOpenAICodexDeviceCode` → `runOpenAICodexDeviceCodeRequest` (`fetch` + `readOpenAICodexDeviceBody` under `AbortSignal.timeout(...)`).
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; production device-code helpers exercised via colocated Vitest against a real hanging `node:http` loopback that sends headers then a partial JSON prefix and never finishes the body. Only `AbortSignal.timeout` duration is shortened for deterministic proof; the production fetch+body composition and error/retry mapping stay unmocked.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Matches the existing 30s OpenAI ChatGPT OAuth token request timeout; uses `AbortSignal.timeout` like GitHub Copilot device-flow request timeouts. Does not migrate this path onto `fetchWithSsrFGuard` in this change.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node 22, product checkout on branch `fix/openai-device-code-request-timeout`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```
 ✓ aborts hung user-code requests instead of waiting forever 1ms
 ✓ retries device authorization polls after a per-request timeout 0ms
 ✓ aborts hung token exchange requests instead of waiting forever 0ms
 ✓ aborts when user-code headers arrive but the body never completes 31ms
 ✓ retries authorization polls after a post-header body stall 43ms
 ✓ aborts when token-exchange headers arrive but the body never completes 43ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
 Duration  1.37s
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 3.53s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Hung user-code and token-exchange fetches abort with `OpenAI device code ... timed out after 30000ms`; a poll `TimeoutError` (including post-header body stall) is retried and the login can still succeed within the overall deadline. Real loopback partial-body stalls exercise production body consumption under the same operation signal.
- **What was not tested:** Live `openclaw models auth login --provider openai --device-code` against a real stalled `auth.openai.com` endpoint.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns
- Single commit on `upstream/main`
